title: Projection normalization of the completed direct-image limit mate
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], schemes $Z,Y$ and a morphism $p:Z\to Y$. Use the actual completed ringed direct image $p_{*,R}$, its strict tower functor, their unbounded right derived functors, the specified strict derived limits $\mathcal L_T$, their projections $\pi_{T,n}$, and the adjunction-conjugate limit isomorphism pushLimit of [def-sp-complete-compactification-limit-comparison]. There exist isomorphisms $w_n:Rp_{*,R}^{\rm Tow}\operatorname{ev}_{Y,n}\simeq\operatorname{ev}_{Z,n}Rp_{*,R}$. On every K-injective strict tower complex $I$, the evaluation of the derived tower direct-image comparison, followed by the exact evaluation localization factor, equals $w_n(QI)$ followed by $Rp_{*,R}$ of the exact source evaluation factor and the finite direct-image comparison on $\operatorname{ev}_nI$. For every derived strict tower $K$, $\operatorname{pushLimit}_K\,\pi_{Y,n}(Rp_{*,R}^{\rm Tow}K)=Rp_{*,R}(\pi_{Z,n}(K))\,w_n(K)^{-1}$. The complex-level normalization is the equality written in compactificationPushLimit, and fixes the specified evaluation isomorphisms before the projection formula. No properness or boundedness is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the ringed-tower direct-image/limit theorem to the completed coefficient morphism of p. Transport its universal derived functors and exact evaluation identifications to the specified ones by the unique localization comparisons. Its K-injective equation gives the first normalization. Its derived limit comparison and pushLimit are conjugates of the same constant-tower pullback square under the composite adjunctions. Uniqueness of adjoints and the composition-unit normalization identify them. Its projection equation, composed with inverse evaluation, is the stated projection identity. These operations preserve strict transitions, and do not test arbitrary derived morphism equality by evaluation.
